QASHANI:92:18/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:92:18/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:92:18/r1.claim: Giving wealth purifies the giver from love of rivals, attachment to otherness, attention to anything besides God, and hidden shirk.
QASHANI:92:18/r1.anchor: متطهرا عن لوث محبة الأنداد وتعلق الأغيار والالتفات إلى ما سوى الله

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.claim: Verses 15–21 explain the traits of those cast into Hell and those shielded from it, together with their reward.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.anchor: An explanation of the character of people who will be thrown into Hell and those who will be shielded from it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.claim: The warning addresses Quraysh: persistent deniers of truth face the blazing fire, while those who spend to attain purity are protected from it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.anchor: people who spend their wealth to attain purity will be shielded from this fire.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.claim: The contrast is between rejecters of God’s Messengers and believers, not degrees of wickedness or piety; conclusive warning leaves Messenger-rejecters no legitimate excuse, making them the most wretched.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.anchor: less pious and the more pious

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r1.claim: Those who heed the Messenger’s warnings, prepare for judgment, and spend to cleanse their wealth are Godfearing; the earliest companions earned the rare ranks of foremost and nearest.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r1.anchor: companions of a Messenger in the initial stages

TUSTARI:92:17-18/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:92:17-18/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:92:17-18/r1.claim: The most Godfearing is the truthful one, identified as Abu Bakr: others gave and feared, but he let go of the perishable and kept the everlasting.
TUSTARI:92:17-18/r1.anchor: الأتقى هو الصديق هو أتقى الناس فإن الناس أعطوا واتقوا وهو لم ير الفاني وأبقى لنفسه الباقي

TUSTARI:92:17-18/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:92:17-18/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:92:17-18/r2.claim: When the Prophet asked what he had kept for himself, Abu Bakr answered: God and His Messenger.
TUSTARI:92:17-18/r2.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ماذا أبقيت لنفسك؟ قال: الله ورسوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says yat azakkā means seeking purity with God without ostentation, or may be a form of tazkiya; the majority read it as a present-tense verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r13.anchor: يتزكى، من الزكاة: أي يطلب أن يكون عند الله زاكيا، لا يريد به رياء ولا سمعة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r1.speaker: الحسن بن علي بن الحسن بن علي بن أبي طالب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r1.claim: Al-Hasan ibn ʿAlī reads yat azakkā with assimilation of tāʾ into zāy.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r2.claim: Yatazakkā is syntactically an accusative circumstantial clause; al-Zamakhsharī's analysis as a replacement for the relative clause is strained.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r2.anchor: ويتزكى في موضع الحال، فموضعه نصب. وأجاز الزمخشري أن لا يكون له موضع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r1.claim: The giver spends his wealth seeking growth and purification before God, without ostentation or reputation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r1.anchor: الذي يؤتي ماله أي يعطيه ويصرفه يتزكى طالبا أن يكون عند الله تعالى زاكيا ناميا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the giver gives his wealth to cleanse himself of sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r2.anchor: أومتطهرا من الذنوب فالجملة نصب على الحال من ضمير يؤتي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r3.claim: The clause may be an accusative circumstantial phrase qualifying the subject of يؤتي.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r3.anchor: فالجملة نصب على الحال من ضمير يؤتي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r4.claim: One proposed parse makes the clause a بدل of the relative clause, leaving it without syntactic position.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r4.anchor: وجوز أن تكون بدلا من الصلة فلا محل لها من الإعراب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r5.claim: Another proposed parse makes the verb alone a بدل of the preceding verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r5.anchor: وجوز أيضا أن يكون الفعل وحده بدلا من الفعل السابق وحده

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r6.claim: Critics object that neither بدل analysis works because the following verb has no matching inflection and is raised independently.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r6.anchor: واعترض كلا الوجهين بأن البدل من قسم التابع المعرف بكل ثان اعرب بإعراب سابقه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r7.claim: The author answers that the first objection can treat inflection as matching whether present or absent, while the second allows prior realization for another reason.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r7.anchor: وأجيب مع الإغماض عما في ذلك التعريف مما نبه على بعضه الرضي أما عن الأول فبان

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r8.speaker: السيد عيسى
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r8.claim: He formulates the rule as a second item being inflected as it would be if it were inflected independently.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r8.anchor: وقال السيد عيسى المراد بقولهم كان ثان أعرب الخ كل ثان أعرب لو لم يكن معربا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r9.claim: A purposive reading supplies لأن before يتزكى; حذف اللام ثم أن can leave the verb raised or accusative.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r9.anchor: وجوز أن يكون يتزكى بتقدير لأن يتزكى متعلقا بيؤتي علة له

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r10.claim: Tarafa's line is cited because أحضر is transmitted both raised and accusative under the proposed ellipsis.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r10.anchor: كما في قول طرفة ألا أيهذا الزاجري أحضر الوغى فقد روي برفع أحضر وبنصبه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r11.claim: Giving wealth here means spending it in righteous and good causes.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r11.anchor: وأيا ما كان يدل الكلام على أن المراد بأيتائه صرفه في وجوه البر والخير

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r12.speaker: الحسن بن علي بن الحسن بن علي بن أبي طالب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r12.claim: He reads يزكي with assimilation of the tāʾ into the zāy.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ابن علي بن الحسن بن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله تعالى عنهميزكي بإدغام التاء في الزاي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r1.claim: The person gives wealth to purify himself before God, without seeking display or reputation; everyone identifies him as Abu Bakr.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r1.anchor: {الذي يؤتي ماله} يعطي ماله {يتزكى} يطلب أن يكون عند الله زاكيا لا رياء ولا سمعة، يعني أبا بكر الصديق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r2.speaker: ابن الزبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r2.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says Abu Bakr bought and freed vulnerable slaves; when his father urged him to buy someone who could protect him, Abu Bakr replied that protection was precisely what he sought.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r2.anchor: قال ابن الزبير: كان أبو بكر يبتاع الضعفة فيعتقهم، فقال أبوه: أي بني لو كنت تبتاع من يمنع ظهرك؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r3.speaker: عروة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r3.claim: Urwa recounts Abu Bakr intervening as Umayya tortured Bilal for saying ‘One, One’; Abu Bakr exchanged a stronger enslaved man for Bilal, then freed six more before Hijra, including Amir ibn Fuhayra, Umm Umays, al-Nahdiyya and her daughter, and a Banu al-Muammal woman. Umm Umays’s sight returned after she rejected the idols.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r3.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه قال: مر به أبو بكر يوما وهم يصنعون به ذلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r6.claim: He gives his wealth to good causes to purify himself; يتزكى is appositional to يؤتي or circumstantial.
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r6.anchor: { يؤتي ماله } يصرفه في مصارف الخير لقوله: { يتزكى } فإنه بدل من { يؤتي }

BINTSHATI:v2p106/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r1.claim: The contrast concerns giving away wealth and hoarding it: the passage says the miser's wealth will not help him and describes the giver as giving wealth to purify himself.
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r1.anchor: وإنه لكذلك، الإعطاء للمال والبخل به، في آيتي الليل

BINTSHATI:v2p116/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r1.claim: The lexical root of zakat means growth, as in fruit becoming good when it ripens and yields its produce.
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r1.anchor: وأصل الزكاة في اللغة النمو، ومنه زكا الثمر بمعنى طاب حين ينضج ويؤتي أكله.

BINTSHATI:v2p116/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r2.claim: In nonphysical use, the word carries an implication of goodness and blessing.
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r2.anchor: ويستعمل في المعنويات بملحظ من الخير والبركة

BINTSHATI:v2p116/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r3.claim: To declare someone pure means to attest to goodness, righteousness, and piety, as in the warning not to praise yourselves.
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r3.anchor: وزكى الشيء أو الشخص شهد له بالخير والصلاح والتقوى

BINTSHATI:v2p116/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r4.claim: Tazkiya also means refinement and purification, illustrated by the Quranic descriptions of messengers purifying people.
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r4.anchor: والتزكية أيضاً التهذيب والتطهير، ومنه في القرآن الكريم آيتا آل عمران 164، والجمعة 2:

BINTSHATI:v2p116/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r5.claim: The religious term zakat is the obligatory wealth a believer gives; God's blessing and reward make the wealth grow, and all 32 Quranic occurrences use this sense.
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r5.anchor: وقد نقلت الزكاة إلى المصطلح الشرعي فيما يؤتيه المؤمن من ماله فريضة، فيزكو المال ببركة الله وثوابه.

BINTSHATI:v2p116/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r6.claim: The verb for purifying wealth in 9:103 resembles the tazakka of this verse, where it accompanies giving wealth.
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r6.anchor: وفي المال أيضاً جاء فعل التزكية بآية التوبة 103: {خذ من أموالهم صدقة

BINTSHATI:v2p116/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r7.claim: Ita' means giving and lexically suggests ease and generosity, like a flood or tree readily yielding fruit; the Quran uses this imagery for giving.
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r7.anchor: والإيتاء هو البذل. وأصله في اللغة الإعطاء مع سهولة ويسر: فالأتى السيل.

BINTSHATI:v2p116/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r8.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r8.claim: The striking Quranic pattern is that zakat is once described with fa'ilun, while its other forms are paired with giving.
BINTSHATI:v2p116/r8.anchor: أنه إذ يعلق الزكاة مرة واحدة بفاعلين في آية المؤمنين 4

BINTSHATI:v2p117/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p117/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p117/r1.claim: Across its Quranic forms, zakat is linked with giving; this supports reading the verse's ita' as giving easily and generously.
BINTSHATI:v2p117/r1.anchor: وبكل هذه الآيات نستأنس في غهم الآية: {الذي يؤتي ماله يتزكى} بملحظ من دلالة الإيتاء على يسر الإعطاء وسماحة البذل.

BINTSHATI:v2p117/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p117/r2.speaker: بعض النحاة
BINTSHATI:v2p117/r2.claim: The usual grammatical analysis treats yatazakka as an accusative circumstantial clause (hal).
BINTSHATI:v2p117/r2.anchor: قالوا: إن جملة {يتزكى} على النصب في موضع الحال.

BINTSHATI:v2p117/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p117/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v2p117/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows yatazakka to have no syntactic position, treating it as a substitute for the relative clause in alladhi yu'ti.
BINTSHATI:v2p117/r3.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري ألا يكون لها موضع من الإعراب، لأنه جعل يتزكى بدلاً من صلة الموصول

BINTSHATI:v2p117/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p117/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v2p117/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan calls al-Zamakhshari's substitute-clause parsing strained; the author prefers the circumstantial analysis as more fitting.
BINTSHATI:v2p117/r4.anchor: وهو كما لاحظ "أبو حيان" إعراب متكلف. والحالية عندنا أولى بالمقام.

BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.claim: The oath's night, daylight, and creation frame divergent earthly endeavors, then contrasting afterlife fates: the denier's fire and the pious giver's satisfaction.
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا النسق من البيان المعجز، يتم الربط بين المقسم به في أول السورة:

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r5.claim: Giving wealth means spending it on good causes, thereby purifying and cultivating the self and replacing bad character with good.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r5.anchor: الذي يؤتي ماله } أي يصرفه في مصارف الخير , ولذلك بينه بقوله تعالى : { يتزكى * } أي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r6.claim: The passage uses reciprocal omission: mentioning denial first implies its opposite later, while mentioning giving later implies its opposite was omitted first.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r6.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك : ذكر التكذيب أولا دليلا على حذف ضده ثانيا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r10.speaker: الزبير بن بكار
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r10.claim: Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār reports that Abū Bakr freed vulnerable Muslims; when his father suggested buying someone to protect him, Abū Bakr said that was precisely his aim.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r10.anchor: نقل البغوي رضي الله تعالى عنه عن الزبير يعني ابن بكاري

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r11.speaker: أبو بكر
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r11.claim: The report attributes to Abū Bakr the reply that he wanted the freed people to protect him, not to purchase a worldly defender.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r11.anchor: كان أبو بكر رضي الله عنه يبتاع الضعفاء فيعتقهم فقال له أبوه : أي بني ! لو كنت تبتاع من يمنع ظهرك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r12.speaker: زهرة
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r12.claim: When Quraysh blamed the idols for a freed woman’s blindness, Zahra rejected their power and her sight returned.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r12.anchor: وأم عميس وزهرة فأصيب بصرها حين أعتقها , فقالت قريش : ما أهذب بصرها إلا اللات والعزى , فقالت : كذبوا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r13.speaker: الزبير بن بكار
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r13.claim: The report lists Abū Bakr’s freeing of al-Nahdiyya, her daughter, and a girl of Banū al-Muʾammal.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r13.anchor: وأعتق النهدية وابنتها وجارية بني المؤمل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r14.claim: A report says Abū Bakr bought Bilāl from Umayya ibn Khalaf while Bilāl was tortured at midday, repeatedly crying “One, One”; the idolaters alleged a prior favor, which revelation refuted.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r14.anchor: وقال : إنه اشترى بلالا من أمية بن خلف استنقاذا له مما كان فيه من العذاب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r1.claim: The promise that Abū Bakr would be pleased connects to the promise that God’s gift will satisfy the Prophet; Abū Bakr is the closest of the community to the Prophet’s station.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه أقرب أمته إلى مقامه لأنه مما وعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه يرضيه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r2.speaker: النبي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r2.claim: The Prophet’s statement that God and the believers would accept only Abū Bakr supports his unique closeness and the contrast between his striving and the worst unbeliever’s.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r2.anchor: يأبى الله والمؤمنون إلا أبا بكر رضي الله عنه

NAHHAS:v5p243/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p243/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p243/r8.claim: The giver gives in order to purify himself of sins.

DURR-FULL:v8p537/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r1.speaker: عروة
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r1.claim: He said Abu Bakr freed seven people tortured for God, including Bilal and ʿAmir ibn Fuhayra; the passage about the most God-fearing was revealed concerning him.
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن عروة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r3.claim: يتزكى is a circumstantial phrase showing that the giver seeks benefit and increased reward, in contrast with idolaters who spend to boast, show off, and pursue corruption; the verb means striving for growth in goodness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r3.anchor: وجملة { يتزكى } حال في ضمير { يؤتي } ، وفائدة الحال التنبيه على أنه يؤتي ماله لقصد النفع والزيادة من الثواب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r4.claim: مال is a generic noun for privately held useful property or its yields, including livestock, land, wells, and trees; some Arabs, such as the people of Yathrib, use it for date palms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r4.anchor: والمال : اسم جنس لما يختص به أحد الناس من أشياء ينتفع بذاتها أو بخراجها وغلتها مثل الأنعام والأرضين والآبار الخاصة والأشجار المختص به أربابها .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r5.claim: The generic construct does not imply all of a person's wealth, so the verse does not require giving everything one owns.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r5.anchor: وليس في إضافة اسم الجنس ما يفيد العموم ، فلا تدل الآية على أنه آتى جميع ماله .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p492/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p492/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p492/r2.claim: Yatazakka means to purify oneself and grow; the verse appears to concern voluntary good works.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p492/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى: يتزكى معناه: يتطهر ويتنمى وظاهر هذه الآية أنه في المندوبات،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p152#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p152#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p152#2/r1.claim: He gives his wealth to purify himself, seeking God's acceptance rather than display or reputation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p152#2/r1.anchor: أي يطلب أن يكون عنه الله زاكيا ولا يطلب الرياء ولا السمعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r2.claim: He spends his wealth in obedience to God to purify himself and what God has granted him, in religion and worldly life.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r2.anchor: أي: يصرف ماله في طاعة ربه؛ ليزكي نفسه وماله وما وهبه الله من دين ودنيا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r6.claim: Abu Bakr gave generously for God's sake and to support the Messenger without owing repayment to anyone; even Arab leaders had received his beneficence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r6.anchor: فكم من دراهم (6) ودنانير (7) بذلها ابتغاء وجه ربه الكريم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r7.claim: The Prophet says the gates of Paradise call to someone who spends two kinds of wealth in God's path; asked whether anyone is called from all gates, he tells Abu Bakr yes and hopes he will be among them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r7.anchor: في الصحيحين أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من أنفق زوجين في سبيل الله دعته خزنة الجنة: يا عبد الله، هذا خير"

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r10.claim: Giving wealth to purify means giving charity and obligatory alms and cleansing oneself through acts of obedience.
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r10.anchor: الذي يؤتي ماله يتزكى أي: يتصدق ويؤدي الواجب، ويتطهر بفعل الطاعات

SAMIN-DURR:92:18/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:18/r1.speaker: الحسن بن علي بن الحسن بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:92:18/r1.claim: The common reading is ‘yatazakka’, the imperfect of tazakka; al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali reads ‘yazakka’, assimilating the tā’ into zāy.
SAMIN-DURR:92:18/r1.anchor: والحسن بن علي بن الحسن بن علي أمير المؤمنين يزكى بإدغام التاء في الزاي

SAMIN-DURR:92:18/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:18/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:92:18/r2.claim: The clause may be a circumstantial from the subject of ‘yu’ti’, meaning he gives while purifying himself through the gift.
SAMIN-DURR:92:18/r2.anchor: أنها في موضع الحال من فاعل " يؤتي " أي: يؤتيه متزكيا به

SAMIN-DURR:92:18/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:18/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:92:18/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows the clause to have no syntactic position and to replace the relative clause of ‘alladhi’; the Shaykh finds this strained.
SAMIN-DURR:92:18/r3.anchor: على أنها بدل من صلة " الذي " ذكرهما الزمخشري. وجعل الشيخ متكلفا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#3/r1.claim: He gives his wealth to the poor and seeks purification before God, without ostentation or desire for reputation; the verb may derive from zakāt.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#3/r1.anchor: من الزكاة أى يطلب أ ن يكون عند الله زاكيا لا يريد به رياء ولا سمعة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#3/r2.claim: If 'purifying himself' is an appositive to 'gives,' it has no syntactic position because it falls inside the relative clause; if circumstantial, it is accusative.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#3/r2.anchor: ويتزكى إن جعلته بدلا من يؤتى فلا محل له لأنه داخل فى حكم الصلة والصلات لا محل لها

QURTUBI-FULL:92:17-18/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:17-18/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:17-18/r3.claim: The person gives wealth seeking purity with God and charity for His sake, without seeking show or reputation.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:17-18/r3.anchor: أي يطلب أن يكون عند الله زاكيا، ولا يطلب بذلك رياء ولا سمعة، بل يتصدق به

QUTB-ZILAL:92:18/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:18/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:18/r1.claim: The most God-fearing gives wealth to purify himself, not to show off or exalt himself; he gives voluntarily, seeks no repayment or thanks, and seeks only his Most High Lord’s pleasure.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:18/r1.anchor: الذي ينفق ماله ليتطهر بإنفاقه ، لا ليرائي به ويستعلي

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r1.speaker: several commentators
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r1.claim: Commentators tell of a Medinan palm owner who snatched fallen dates from a poor family's children and refused the Prophet's offer of a Paradise palm; another man paid forty palms, donated the tree, and the Prophet gave it to the family. The refusal maps to vv. 15–16, the gift to vv. 18–21.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r1.anchor: Several commentators say that the whole of this sūrah was revealed in reference to a Muslim of Madinah who had a palm tree

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r2.claim: If this is an early Makkan sūrah, the palm-tree story likely is not its occasion; the verses instead generally condemn those who rejected Muhammad as prophet.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r2.anchor: If, however, this is an early Makkan sūrah, as some maintain

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r3.claim: Giving charity in God's name purifies both the giver and the wealth; tazakkā shares an etymological root with zakāh.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r3.anchor: one purifies both oneself and one’s wealth when one gives charity in the Name of God. To purify translates tazakkā, which is etymologically related to the Quranic word for alms, zakāh

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r4.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r4.claim: Others say vv. 17–21 praise Abū Bakr, who bought and freed weak slaves; when his father asked why he did not buy stronger defenders, he said he sought no defense.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r4.anchor: others say that vv. 18–21 were revealed about the first Caliph, Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, who used to buy weak slaves and then free them

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r5.claim: One revelation account says Bilāl was tortured after desecrating the Kaʿbah idols, kept testifying to God's oneness, and the Prophet assured him that the One would save him.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r5.anchor: One account of the revelation of these verses states that, upon embracing Islam, Bilāl, who was a slave of one ʿAbd Allāh ibn Judan

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r6.claim: In that account Abū Bakr bought Bilāl for gold after the Prophet told him Bilāl was tortured for God; the idolaters alleged he acted to repay a favor, prompting vv. 19–21.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r6.anchor: The Prophet came upon this and said to him, “The One will save you!” He then informed Abū Bakr, saying,“Bilāl is being tortured for the sake of God!

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r7.claim: Bilāl later became the first to lead the call to prayer and one of the Prophet's personal treasurers.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r7.anchor: Bilāl later became the first to lead the call to prayer

TAB:92:18/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:18/r1.speaker: author
TAB:92:18/r1.claim: The God-fearing person gives wealth toward the obligations God imposed, thereby purifying himself of sins.
TAB:92:18/r1.anchor: الذي يعطي ماله في الدنيا في حقوق الله التي ألزمه إياها ،   يتزكى :  يعني :  يتطهر بإعطائه ذلك من ذنوبه

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:18:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:18:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:18:anmerkung/r1.claim: Tazakkā is related to zakka/tazakkā in the note on 91:9; sura 91 also shares the term al-ašqā.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:18:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zu den Verben zakkā bzw. tazakkā vgl. die Anmerkung zu 91:9. Q 91 hat mit dem vorliegenden Text auch den Begriff al-ʾašqā gemeinsam

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura develops two antitheses: behavior and recompense for the saved and damned, first in verses 5–13 and then in verses 14–21.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.anchor: Es folgen zwei Antithesen (V. 5–13 und V. 14–21), welche die Verhaltensweisen und Jenseitsschicksale von Seligen und Verdammten miteinander kontrastieren

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.claim: The final stanza reverses the earlier order of saved and damned; the outer blessed sections are linked by ittaqā in verse 5 and ʾatqā in verse 17.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.anchor: Zum einen wird die Reihenfolge Seliger – Verdammter (V. 5–7 und V. 8–11) jetzt invertiert (V. 14–16 Verdammter, V. 17–20 Seliger)

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.claim: The stanza halves mirror one another: earlier behavior lists precede reward or warning, while the final warning and promise precede each group's worldly conduct.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.anchor: In V. 5–7 und V. 8–11 ging zunächst ein Tugend- bzw. Lasterkatalog voraus, auf den dann jeweils ein Drohwort bzw. eine Verheißung folgten

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r6.claim: The longer, central portrait of the pious clarifies that generosity is for ethical purification, not repayment of worldly favors, and is directed toward the Lord's face through a biblical metaphor.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r6.anchor: Der Gottesfürchtige gibt um seiner ethischen Reinheit willen (V. 18) und nicht aufgrund weltlicher Beweggründe wie der Rückerstattung empfangener Wohltaten (V. 19)

TABATABAI:92:15-20/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:15-20/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:15-20/r4.claim: The pious person gives and spends wealth to make himself grow in purity.
TABATABAI:92:15-20/r4.anchor: الذي يعطي وينفق ماله يطلب بذلك أن ينمو نماء صالحا

TABRISI:92:2-3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:2-3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:92:2-3/r7.claim: Yatazakkā is accusative as a circumstantial phrase, or its position can reflect an omitted أن; deleting أن is illustrated by Ṭarafa's line.
TABRISI:92:2-3/r7.anchor: ويتزكى في موضع نصب على الحال ويجوز أن يكون منصوب الموضع أو مرفوعا

THALABI:v10p218#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p218#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p218#2/r6.claim: The one who gives wealth to purify himself is identified in reports as Abu Bakr; he purchased and freed enslaved Muslims who were tortured for their faith.
THALABI:v10p218#2/r6.anchor: أن أبا بكر رضي الله عنه أعتق من كان يعذب في الله: بلال وعامر بن فهيرة والنهدية

THALABI:v10p219/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p219/r1.speaker: عروة عن أبيه
THALABI:v10p219/r1.claim: Abu Bakr freed Bilal and other persecuted people; the passage is said to concern him, and he spent all of his forty thousand in charity.
THALABI:v10p219/r1.anchor: وأما بلال فاشتراه، وهو مدفون بالحجارة، فقالوا: لو أبيت إلا أوقية واحدة لبعناك

THALABI:v10p219/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p219/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
THALABI:v10p219/r2.claim: He says Abu Bakr bought and freed vulnerable slaves; when his father advised buying someone to protect him, Abu Bakr said he was pursuing his own aim, and the verse was revealed about him.
THALABI:v10p219/r2.anchor: كان أبو بكر يبتاع الضعفة فيعتقهم، فقال له أبوه: يا بني لو كنت تبتاع من يمنع ظهرك

THALABI:v10p219/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p219/r3.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p219/r3.claim: He recounts Bilal's monotheistic defiance while being tortured, the Prophet's reassurance, and Abu Bakr's purchase of Bilal with gold.
THALABI:v10p219/r3.anchor: وهو يقول: أحدا أحد، فمر به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: ينجيك أحد أحد

THALABI:v10p219/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p219/r4.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
THALABI:v10p219/r4.claim: He recounts that Abu Bakr obtained Bilal by trading him for Nustas, a wealthy enslaved man who refused Islam; God then declared Abu Bakr's emancipation was solely for His sake, to be repaid in the hereafter.
THALABI:v10p219/r4.anchor: إلا لكن ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى ولسوف يرضى بثواب الله في العقبى عوضا مما فعل في الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p89/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p89/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p89/r1.claim: He gives wealth to become pure in God's sight and does not seek ostentation or public praise.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p89/r1.anchor: يطلب أن يكون عند الله زاكيا لا يطلب بذلك رياء ولا سمعة

WAHIDI-QT:92:18/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:18/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:18/r1.claim: He gives his wealth seeking purity with God, not showing off or seeking reputation.
WAHIDI-QT:92:18/r1.anchor: يطلب أن يكون عند الله زاكيا ولا يطلب رياء ولا سمعة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.claim: The lām emphasizing God's ownership suits the surah's repeated focus on wealth and possession; unlike this context, the wealth-free context of 53:25 omits it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.anchor: فسياق الآيات في سورة الليل جاء كله في الأموال وامتلاكها والتصرف فيها

ELMALILI:92:12-21/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r9.claim: The most God-fearing gives wealth to purify himself, grow spiritually, and prosper; alternatively, the verb describes giving in order to become purified before God.
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r9.anchor: O etkā ki malını verir tezekkî eder temizlenir, tefeyyüz eyler, felah bulur. Yahut “yetezekkâ” hâl olduğuna göre

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.claim: Others say verses 5–19 were revealed about Abu Bakr; regardless of a specific occasion, the message and rulings are general.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.anchor: bazıları ise 5-19. âyetlerin (bk. Elmalılı, VIII, 5881), müşriklerin işkence ettiği köleleri satın alıp âzat ederek hürriyetlerine kavuşturan Hz. Ebû Bekir hakkında indiğini söylemişlerdir. Âyetler böyle bir özel olay üzerine gelmiş olsa da, hükümleri ve mesajları geneldir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r4.claim: A pious believer need not receive a favor or gain before helping; all blessings come from God, and good should be done for God's approval alone.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r4.anchor: mümin, her türlü nimetin yalnızca Allah’ın bir lutfu olduğuna, iyiliklerin de ilke olarak bir çıkar hesabıyla değil, sadece Allah rızâsı için yapılması gerektiğine inanır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.claim: After warning of the blazing fire in verse 14, verses 17–20 describe giving for God's sake without owing anyone, spiritual purification, and being kept from the fire.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.anchor: 14. âyette muhataplar “alev alev yanan ateş”e karşı uyarıldıktan sonra 17-20. âyetlerde, birine borçlu olmadıkları, kimsenin kendilerinde bir hakkı bulunmadığı halde bile

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p391/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p391/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p391/r2.claim: Abu Bakr is one instance within the general description of a giver seeking purification; mentioning this unusual case does not restrict the general wording.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p391/r2.anchor: وهذا شبيه بذكر بعض أفراد العام وهو لا يخصص للعموم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r4.claim: Yatazakka means seeking purity with God without ostentation, or derives from the form for paying alms.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r4.anchor: يتزكى } من الزكاء . أي : يطلب أن يكون عند الله زاكيا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r5.claim: Yatazakka may be an appositional part of the relative clause and have no case, or a circumstantial clause attached to the pronoun in yu'ti.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r5.anchor: إن جعلته بدلا من { يؤتى } فلا محل له

QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.claim: An alternative contextual account identifies the giver as Abu al-Dahdah and the miser as the Ansari palm owner; it maps ease to Paradise, hardship to Hell, and death to loss of wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.anchor: { فأما من أعطى واتقى } يعني أبا الدحداح. { وصدق بالحسنى } أي بالثواب

QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r3.claim: The most pious one is Abu al-Dahdah, who gave the palm’s price to purify himself.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r3.anchor: { وسيجنبها الأتقى } يعني أبا الدحداح. { الذى يؤتي ماله يتزكى } في ثمن تلك النخلة

RAZI-FULL:v31p186/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p186/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v31p186/r1.claim: Al-Kashshaf says yat azakkā may be an appositive of 'gives,' with no syntactic case inside the relative clause, or a circumstantial accusative modifying the subject of 'gives.'
RAZI-FULL:v31p186/r1.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) في محل : { يتزكى } وجهان

RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r3.claim: The pious giver is not repaying an earlier gift or favor, which would merely settle a debt; reward is due because he gives in response to God's command.
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r3.anchor: لا يؤتيه مكافأة على هدية أو نعمة سالفة

THALABI:v10p220/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r1.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v10p220/r1.claim: A man refused the Prophet’s offer of a date palm in Paradise for his palm that dropped fruit into a neighbor’s yard; Abū al-Daḥdāḥ bought and donated it, and the Prophet transferred it to the neighbor. The account identifies them with the surah’s contrasting figures.
THALABI:v10p220/r1.anchor: عطاء قال: كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة، وكان له جار، فكان يسقط من بلحها في دار جاره

THALABI:v10p220/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p220/r5.claim: Abū al-Daḥdāḥ is the God-fearing person kept away from the Fire because he gives his wealth to purify himself, seeking only his Lord’s face rather than repaying a favor.
THALABI:v10p220/r5.anchor: وسيجنبها الأتقى يعني أبا الدحداح الذي يؤتي ماله يتزكى يعني أبا الدحداح وما لأحد عنده من نعمة تجزى

BURHAN:v4p90/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p90/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p90/r2.claim: In an adjective and similar constructions, agreement usually follows the preceding word’s form; agreement by meaning rather than form is rarer.
BURHAN:v4p90/r2.anchor: ثم الأكثر في نعتها وغيرها مرافقة اللفظ

ITQAN:v1p91/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p91/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p91/r1.claim: By consensus, 92:17–18 was revealed specifically about Abu Bakr; its wording is not general.
ITQAN:v1p91/r1.anchor: فإنها نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق بالإجماع

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p161/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p161/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p161/r3.claim: A positive imperfect verbal circumstantial clause generally appears without wāw, whether its subject is the person whose state is described or someone related to that person; he cites this verse alongside 74:6 and 7:186, as well as poetic examples.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p161/r3.anchor: وقوله تعالى : ( ﴿ وسيجنبها الأتقى الذي يؤتي ماله يتزكى ﴾ )

ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r1.claim: The one who gives seeks purity and standing with God, without seeking ostentation or reputation.
ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r1.anchor: أي يطلب أن يكون عند الله زاكياً ، لا يريد به رياء ولا سمعة

ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r2.claim: The verb may also be analyzed as the form yatafaʿʿalu derived from zakah.

ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r3.claim: The majority read يتزكى as the imperfect of تزكى.

ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r4.speaker: الحسن بن علي بن الحسن بن علي بن أبي طالب
ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r4.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib reads with the tā assimilated into the zāy.
ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن عليّ بن الحسن بن عليّ بن أبي طالب رضي الله تعالى عنهم : بإدغام التاء في الزاي

ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r5.claim: In the usual parsing, يتزكى is an accusative circumstantial clause.
ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r5.anchor: ويتزكى في موضع الحال ، فموضعه نصب

ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows no syntactic position by treating يتزكى as a substitute for يؤتي in the relative clause; Abū Ḥayyān calls this parsing strained.
ABUHAYYAN:92:18/r6.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري أن لا يكون له موضع من الإعراب لأنه جعله بدلاً من صلة الذي ، وهو { يؤتي } ، قاله : وهو إعراب متكلف

ALUSI:92:18/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:18/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:18/r1.claim: He gives and spends his wealth.

ALUSI:92:18/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:18/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:18/r2.claim: He gives seeking wealth that is pure and growing with God, without ostentation or reputation, or seeking purification from sins.
ALUSI:92:18/r2.anchor: طالباً أن يكون عند الله تعالى زاكياً نامياً لا يريد به رياء ولا سمعة

ALUSI:92:18/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:18/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:18/r3.claim: The clause is an accusative circumstantial qualifier of the pronoun in yuʾtī.
ALUSI:92:18/r3.anchor: فالجملة نصب على الحال من ضمير يؤتي

ALUSI:92:18/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:18/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:18/r4.claim: Alternative parses make the clause a substitute for the relative clause, or the verb alone a substitute for the preceding verb; both are challenged because the relative clause has no case ending to follow and the verb's nominative is independently due to its being ungoverned.
ALUSI:92:18/r4.anchor: وجوز أن تكون بدلاً من الصلة فلا محل لها من الإعراب

ALUSI:92:18/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:18/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:18/r5.claim: Replies allow follower status to mean same case when available or matching its presence or absence; calling an uninflected word a follower may be figurative due to resemblance, and a case may be intended even when independently licensed. Al-Sayyid ʿĪsā defines it as a second word that would be inflected if it were inflectable.
ALUSI:92:18/r5.anchor: وقيل إطلاق التابع على ذلك ونحوه من الحرف والفعل الغير المعرب مجاز

ALUSI:92:18/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:18/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:18/r6.claim: Another parse supplies li-an before yatizakkā as the purpose of giving, deleting both lām and an; the verb may be raised or subjunctive, as in two transmitted readings of Ṭarafa's line.
ALUSI:92:18/r6.anchor: وجوز أن يكون يتزكى بتقدير لأن يتزكى متعلقاً بيؤتي علة له

ALUSI:92:18/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:18/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:18/r7.claim: On any parse, the wealth is spent in charitable and good causes.
ALUSI:92:18/r7.anchor: وأياً ما كان يدل الكلام على أن المراد بأيتائه صرفه في وجوه البر والخير

ALUSI:92:18/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:18/r8.speaker: الحسن بن علي بن الحسن بن علي
ALUSI:92:18/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī reads yazakkā, assimilating the tāʾ into the zāy.
ALUSI:92:18/r8.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن علي بن الحسن بن علي

BAGHAWI:92:18/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:18/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:92:18/r1.claim: He gives his wealth seeking purity with God, without ostentation or desire for reputation; all identify him as Abu Bakr.
BAGHAWI:92:18/r1.anchor: يتزكى } يطلب أن يكون عند الله زاكياً لا رياء ولا سمعة ،   يعني أبا بكر الصديق

BAGHAWI:92:18/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:18/r2.speaker: ابن الزبير
BAGHAWI:92:18/r2.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says Abu Bakr bought and freed enslaved weak people; when his father suggested buying stronger allies, Abu Bakr answered that he sought protection for his own back, and the passage through the end of the sura was revealed.
BAGHAWI:92:18/r2.anchor: قال ابن الزبير : كان أبو بكر يبتاع الضعفة فيعتقهم ،   فقال أبوه : أي بني لو كنت تبتاع من يمنع ظهرك ؟

BAGHAWI:92:18/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:18/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
BAGHAWI:92:18/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Bilal ibn Rabah, son of Hamama, was tortured by Umayya ibn Khalaf in Mecca's noonday heat, pinned beneath a boulder and told to renounce Muhammad; he kept saying Ahad, Ahad.
BAGHAWI:92:18/r3.anchor: وذكر محمد بن إسحاق قال : كان بلال لبعض بني جمع وهو بلال بن رباح واسم أمه حمامة

BAGHAWI:92:18/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:18/r4.speaker: هشام بن عروة عن أبيه
BAGHAWI:92:18/r4.claim: Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, reports Abu Bakr challenging Umayya over Bilal's torture, exchanging a strong enslaved man for Bilal, and freeing him.
BAGHAWI:92:18/r4.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق ،   عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه قال : مر به أبو بكر يوماً وهم يصنعون به ذلك

BAGHAWI:92:18/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:18/r5.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
BAGHAWI:92:18/r5.claim: Ibn Ishaq lists six other people Abu Bakr freed before the migration: Amir ibn Fuhayra, Umm Umays, Zahra, al-Nahdiyya and her daughter, and a girl of Banu al-Muammal.
BAGHAWI:92:18/r5.anchor: ثم أعتق معه على الإسلام قبل أن يهاجر ست رقاب ،   بلال سابعهم وهم : عامر بن فهيرة

BAGHAWI:92:18/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:18/r6.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
BAGHAWI:92:18/r6.claim: Ibn Ishaq adds that Quraysh blamed the idols for Zahra's impaired sight, but she denied their power and her sight returned; Abu Bakr bought al-Nahdiyya and her daughter despite their mistress's refusal, and freed a tortured Banu al-Muammal girl.
BAGHAWI:92:18/r6.anchor: فأصيب بصرها وأعتقها ،   فقالت قريش : ما أذهب بصرها إلا اللات والعزى فقالت : كذبوا وبيت الله

BAYDAWI:92:18/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:18/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:18/r1.claim: He spends his wealth on good causes.

BAYDAWI:92:18/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:18/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:18/r2.claim: Yatazakkā can be an appositive to yuʾtī or a circumstantial qualifier of its subject.
BAYDAWI:92:18/r2.anchor: لقوله يتزكى فإنه بدل من يؤتي أو حال من فاعله

BIQAI:92:18/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:18/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:18/r1.claim: He spends his wealth on good purposes, thereby cleansing and developing himself, avoiding base traits and adopting good ones; this contrasts with denial and turning away.

BIQAI:92:18/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:18/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:18/r2.claim: The verse uses ḥatbāk: mentioning denial first implies omission of its opposite second, while mentioning giving wealth second implies omission of its opposite first.
BIQAI:92:18/r2.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك : ذكر التكذيب أولاً دليلاً على حذف ضده ثانياً

IBNASHUR:92:15/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:15/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:15/r10.claim: The relative clauses describing the most wretched and most pious signal that their respective actions cause the stated outcome.
IBNASHUR:92:15/r10.anchor: للإيذان بأن للصلة تسببا في الحكم

IBNASHUR:92:18/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:18/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:18/r1.claim: Yatazakkā is a circumstantial clause attached to the pronoun in yuʾtī; it shows that he gives seeking benefit and increased reward.
IBNASHUR:92:18/r1.anchor: وفائدة الحال التنبيه على أنه يؤتي ماله لقصد النفع والزيادة من الثواب

IBNASHUR:92:18/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:18/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:18/r2.claim: This motive contrasts with polytheists who give for pride, ostentation, mischief, and debauchery.
IBNASHUR:92:18/r2.anchor: المشركين الذي يؤتون المال للفخر والرياء والمفاسد والفجور

IBNASHUR:92:18/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:18/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:18/r3.claim: Tazakkī means seeking zakāʾ, growth in goodness.

IBNASHUR:92:18/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:18/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:18/r4.claim: Māl is a generic noun for what someone owns and benefits from directly or through yield, such as livestock, land, private wells, and trees.
IBNASHUR:92:18/r4.anchor: من أشياء ينتفع بذاتها أو بخراجها وغلتها

IBNASHUR:92:18/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:18/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:18/r5.claim: Some Arabs, including the people of Yathrib, use māl for date palms.
IBNASHUR:92:18/r5.anchor: ويطلق عند بعض العرب مثل أهل يثرب على النخيل

IBNASHUR:92:18/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:18/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:18/r6.claim: The generic noun in this construction does not imply totality, so the verse does not say that he gave all his wealth.
IBNASHUR:92:18/r6.anchor: فلا تدل الآية على أنه آتى جميع ماله

IBNATIYYA:92:18/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:18/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:18/r1.claim: Yatazakkā means to purify oneself and to grow or increase.
IBNATIYYA:92:18/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى [ يتزكى ] معناه : يتطهر ويتنمى

IBNATIYYA:92:18/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:18/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:18/r2.claim: The apparent sense is that this giving concerns recommended acts.
IBNATIYYA:92:18/r2.anchor: وظاهر هذا الإتيان أنه في المندوبات

IBNKATHIR:92:18/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:18/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:92:18/r1.claim: He spends wealth in obedience to his Lord, purifying himself, his wealth, and what God granted him in religion and worldly life.
IBNKATHIR:92:18/r1.anchor: أي : يصرف ماله في طاعة ربه

KASHSHAF:92:18/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:18/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:18/r1.claim: From zakāʾ, it means seeking to be pure in God's sight, without seeking ostentation or reputation.
KASHSHAF:92:18/r1.anchor: أي : يطلب أن يكون عند الله زاكيا

KASHSHAF:92:18/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:18/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:18/r2.claim: Alternatively, it is the verb form meaning to give zakāh.

KASHSHAF:92:18/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:18/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:18/r3.claim: Yatazakkā can be an appositive within the relative clause and then has no syntactic position, or a circumstantial accusative describing the subject of yuʾtī.
KASHSHAF:92:18/r3.anchor: إن جعلته بدلا من { يؤتي } فلا محل له

NASAFI:92:18/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:18/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:18/r1.claim: He gives his wealth to the poor, seeking purity before God rather than showing off or seeking fame.
NASAFI:92:18/r1.anchor: { الذى يُؤْتِى مَالَهُ } للفقراء { يتزكى } من الزكاء أي يطلب أن يكون عند الله زاكياً لا يريد به رياء ولا سمعة

NASAFI:92:18/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:18/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:18/r2.claim: If “purifying himself” substitutes for “gives,” it has no syntactic case because it falls within the relative clause.
NASAFI:92:18/r2.anchor: و { يتزكى } إن جعلته بدلاً من { يؤتى } فلا محل له لأنه داخل في حكم الصلة

NASAFI:92:18/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:18/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:18/r3.claim: If taken as a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in “he gives,” it is accusative.
NASAFI:92:18/r3.anchor: وإن جعلته حالاً من الضمير في { يؤتى } فمحله النصب

QURTUBI:92:18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:18/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:18/r1.claim: The God-fearing person gives wealth seeking purity with God and His approval, without ostentation or desire for reputation.
QURTUBI:92:18/r1.anchor: ثم وصف الأتقى فقال : " الذي يؤتي ماله يتزكى " أي يطلب أن يكون عند اللّه زاكيا

RAZI:92:17/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:17/r3.speaker: الشيعة
RAZI:92:17/r3.claim: Al-Razi says the Shīʿa reject the Abū Bakr report and identify ʿAlī, linking the giving of wealth with the verse about alms given while bowing.
RAZI:92:17/r3.anchor: واعلم أن الشيعة بأسرهم ينكرون هذه الرواية ، ويقولون : إنها نزلت في حق علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام والدليل عليه قوله تعالى : { ويؤتون الزكاة وهم راكعون }

RAZI:92:17/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:17/r9.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI:92:17/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī gives two parses for yatazakkā: a substitute for yuʾtī with no syntactic case, or an accusative circumstantial phrase attached to the pronoun in yuʾtī.
RAZI:92:17/r9.anchor: قال صاحب «الكشاف » في محل : { يتزكى } وجهان : إن جعلت بدلا من يؤتي فلا محل له ، لأنه داخل في حكم الصلة
